title: Mahershala Ali Says Two Oscars Do Not Guarantee Better Roles
excerpt:
Mahershala Ali says two Academy Awards offer no guarantee of finding the right part.
The actor discusses scarce scripts, casting realities and representation in Hollywood.
body_md:
Mahershala Ali has reflected on the difference between awards recognition and the everyday realities of finding meaningful work in Hollywood. Speaking on the 7pm in Brooklyn podcast, the two-time Academy Award winner explained that prestigious trophies do not automatically translate into scripts being written for him, projects being approved with him in mind, or casting offers that suit his strengths.

Ali sees an Oscar as recognition for work already completed rather than a permanent advantage in the marketplace. He pointed out that numerous gifted performers have never won an Academy Award and are still seeking substantial material. The central problem, in his view, is not a shortage of talent but a shortage of roles that offer the right combination of writing, character and opportunity.

Even an excellent screenplay may not contain a character that fits a particular actor. Producers and writers may also develop a project with somebody else in mind from the outset. Ali stressed that casting is not simply a contest in which the most decorated performer wins. If a studio is not developing the kind of story in which he can participate, additional awards would not change that situation. His remarks describe the practical limits of acclaim rather than a rejection of the Academy or the value of his wins.

The conversation also turned to diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives and the effect their rollback may have on production decisions. Ali argued that reduced pressure to reflect the breadth of society can influence which projects receive approval. In his assessment, executives may gravitate toward people and experiences familiar to their own professional circles when broader representation is no longer a priority. These comments were his interpretation of industry dynamics, not an announcement of a new studio policy.

At the same time, the actor does not want to be defined only through the lens of diversity-focused projects. He wants compelling characters and strong storytelling, without being treated as an unusual category of performer. For Ali, the aim is to have his work considered on its artistic merits while acknowledging that opportunities are shaped by who gets to make decisions about stories.

Ali won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for Moonlight at the 2017 ceremony and again for Green Book in 2019. His latest performance in Bassam Tariq's Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother has also generated awards discussion. His new comments should not be confused with an announcement that he is leaving acting or that a particular role has been withdrawn. They offer a candid perspective on why even a celebrated career cannot eliminate uncertainty about the next good project.
seo_title: Mahershala Ali on Why Two Oscars Cannot Secure Roles
seo_description: The two-time Oscar winner discusses casting, the scarcity of strong scripts and representation in Hollywood.
